denied.title: Access denied
denied.text: User {user} has no access to OpenWrt-Admin.
denied.hint: An administrator can add them in the add-on configuration to read_access (read-only) or full_access.
setup.key_text: The add-on logs in to the APs and the router with this key (reading via ubus, changes via uci). Add it to every device:
setup.key_note: /etc/dropbear/authorized_keys survives sysupgrade. After sysupgrade -n add it again (or put it in a first-boot script).
setup.devices_text: APs, user, intervals and the DHCP router are set in Home Assistant: Settings → Apps (Add-ons) → OpenWrt-Admin → Configuration.
setup.users_text: Login is handled by Home Assistant; the add-on decides what each HA user may do.
setup.no_roles_warning: No roles configured: every HA user who opens the panel has full access (reboot, apk, SSIDs). Set full_access and read_access in the add-on configuration.
setup.users_hint: Use the HA username (Settings → People → Users) or the display name; case-insensitive.
setup.lang_source.auto: automatic, from Home Assistant / the browser
setup.display_hint: Defaults for everyone are set in the add-on configuration (refresh_interval, language). The choices here apply to this browser only.
setup.api_text: The current state is also available as JSON:
router.confirm_reboot: Reboot the router {ap}? The whole network and the internet will be down for 1–2 minutes.
router.confirm_upgrade: Run {pkg} upgrade on the router {ap}? Upgrading packages can break networking; sysupgrade is safer.
router.actions_note: Rebooting the router takes the whole network and internet down (Home Assistant keeps running but cannot reach anything outside the LAN for a moment).
map.title: Network map
map.note: Lines show logical connections: the AP is in the router's network and carries the listed VLANs. Wired devices and APs connected through another AP are detected from the AP switch MAC table (swconfig arl_table); where the switch cannot provide it, they stay under the router. Unmanaged switches in between are not visible. VLAN IDs come from device names (eth0.30, br-lan.10), bridge members and uci.
